title: Beneath the Surface: What We Overlook When We Talk About Agent Evolution

details.title: Beneath the Surface: What We Overlook When We Talk About Agent Evolution
details.abstract: Does a higher benchmark score really mean an agent is getting better? 🤔 In our paper, we go beyond surface-level benchmark evaluations to investigate what actually happens during agent evolution and why improvements do not always translate into better agents. We systematically study agent evolution from three perspectives, Phenomenology, Generalization, and Mechanisms , and further dissect four key stages: Select, Analyze, Mutate, and Gate . Building on these insights, we introduce EvoAudit and Audit-Guided Evolution (AGE) , moving toward more reliable, evidence-driven agent self-improvement. 💻 Code: https://github.com/simple-agent-lab/RSIHub

title: EvoWorld: Towards Out-of-Sight World Evolution in Generative Video Models

details.title: EvoWorld: Towards Out-of-Sight World Evolution in Generative Video Models
details.abstract: We are excited to introduce EvoWorld, a video generation framework for out-of-sight world evolution. EvoWorld combines a VLM brain with a visual renderer, enabling off-screen entities to remain active participants in an evolving world. Within a bidirectional autoregressive paradigm, EvoWorld supports event-triggered world evolution, subject and scene revisitation, and out-of-sight dynamics rendering through model reasoning.

title: Video-Coder: Reinforcing Agentic Coding for Video Generation

details.title: Video-Coder: Reinforcing Agentic Coding for Video Generation
details.abstract: Recent years have witnessed remarkable progress in video generation in terms of visual quality and temporal consistency. However, generating videos with precise spatial structure, coherent motion dynamics, and controllable scene composition remains challenging. In this paper, we introduce Video-Coder, the first attempt to train a code-driven video generation agent, which autonomously writes and executes code to construct a dynamic 3D scene (Draft Video) that provides structure and motion signals to downstream video generators. To support this paradigm, we design a dedicated data pipeline and curate two high-quality datasets, Video-Coder-SFT-6k and Video-Coder-RL-2k, which contain diverse prompts and ground-truth reference videos. We further develop the Video- Coder Harness, a unified interactive environment integrating code execution, 3D scene rendering, and execution feedback for agent training and inference. We then train Video-Coder with SFT fol- lowed by harness-native agentic reinforcement learning with dual reward feedback, which combines execution-based and video-based rewards. Additionally, we design an annealing training strategy that gradually reduces the execution reward over time, allowing the model to rely more on the video reward in the later training stages. Experiments show that Video-Coder achieves significant gains, improving Minimax-H3 by approximately 7 points on PhyGenBench and 24 points on VBench-2.0. We hope this work can serve as an open foundation for coding agents in video generation, and we fully open-source our data, models, and code

title: Exploring Weight-Space Programming: Capabilities, Generalization, and Limitations

details.title: Exploring Weight-Space Programming: Capabilities, Generalization, and Limitations
details.abstract: We systematically evaluate Weight-Space Programming through 16 editing trajectories across seven benchmarks and two model scales. Our results show uneven cross-task transfer, substantial variation across independent searches, and more limited gains on the larger model. Feedback and discussion are welcome.

title: Confucius4-R2T2: A Stable-Prefix Streaming ASR Model for Real Real-Time Transcription

details.title: Confucius4-R2T2: A Stable-Prefix Streaming ASR Model for Real Real-Time Transcription
details.abstract: Excited to share Confucius4-R2T2 , our stable-prefix streaming ASR model designed for real-time applications! Unlike conventional streaming ASR systems that repeatedly revise partial transcripts, R2T2 produces append-only, stable text that downstream systems such as voice agents and simultaneous translators can consume immediately. The key idea is Longest Stable Prefix (LSP) supervision, which enables us to transform a full-context ASR model into a streaming one through post-training, without architectural modifications. Built on Qwen3-ASR-1.7B, R2T2 achieves near-offline recognition accuracy with low emission latency, supports configurable streaming chunk sizes, and demonstrates promising cross-lingual generalization. We've made the model and implementation publicly available: 🤗 Model: https://huggingface.co/netease-youdao/Confucius4-R2T2 💻 GitHub: https://github.com/netease-youdao/Confucius4-R2T2 🎙️ Live demo: https://r2t2.youdao.com/demo We'd love to hear your feedback and see what the community builds with it!

title: The Last Mile to the Real World: Agent-Native Primitives as Reusable Building Blocks for Solving Real-World Tasks

details.title: The Last Mile to the Real World: Agent-Native Primitives as Reusable Building Blocks for Solving Real-World Tasks
details.abstract: How can AI agents reliably solve real-world tasks end to end? We introduce Agent-Native Primitives, reusable building blocks that equip tools, code, knowledge, and other resources with their own LLM-powered experts. Building on this idea, HEELO dynamically composes task-specific agent harnesses from eight families of primitives. Across 20+ benchmarks and 46 real-world tasks, HEELO substantially improves agent performance. On our real-world tasks, connecting existing agent systems to HEELO increases completed tasks from 9 to 39 for Claude Code and from 9 to 35 for Codex.

title: Sketchpad: certified exact arithmetic with a small vision-language model

details.title: Sketchpad: certified exact arithmetic with a small vision-language model
details.abstract: Author here. Can a small model be proven exact at arithmetic on inputs of every length? 🧮 The theory If each step of a model reads only a bounded view of an external memory, exactness at all lengths reduces to exactness on a finite set of views . Proved in Lean, along with: Necessity: once steps can also read earlier steps, no finite test suffices . Robustness: the guarantee survives bounded numerical error. Composition: certified procedures stay certified when combined. ⚙️ In practice Qwen3.5-0.8B + a small adapter passes all 2,446 views on a laptop GPU, in the browser. It is certified for + − × ÷ √ gcd at any length. 220 pre-registered problems Score Sketchpad (0.8B) 220 GPT-6.1 Sol · Claude Opus 5.5 · Gemini 4 Argon 217 · 216 · 207 Five open-weight models 149–199 Qwen3.5-27B · Qwen3.5-0.8B (base) 121 · 23 On 1,000-digit sums : Sketchpad 20/20; frontier models 19, 17, 9; every open-weight model ≤ 2. 🔗 Live demo · Code

title: WorldFoundry: Towards Unified Infrastructure for World Intelligence

details.title: WorldFoundry: Towards Unified Infrastructure for World Intelligence
details.abstract: Visual generative models increasingly blur the line between synthesizing observations and simulating environments. Yet visual plausibility alone does not constitute successful world modeling: compelling outputs may lack persistent state, physical dynamics, or causally consistent responses to interactions. The absence of a shared operational basis, together with perception-centric benchmarks and fragmented workflows, obscures the distinction between generative foundation models and generative world models and hinders reproducible assessment of dynamics, controllability, and interactive utility. We define a generative world model as a predictive dynamical system that maintains a persistent, history-conditioned representation of an environment, updates that representation in response to actions or interventions, and generates temporally coherent trajectories that reflect outcomes under observed and counterfactual interventions. From this definition, we derive an intelligence-oriented framework spanning perceptual grounding, persistent state modeling, controllable transformation, dynamics-aware prediction, and closed-loop interaction. We further present WorldFoundry, open-source infrastructure for reproducible inference and evaluation across video, 3D and 4D, embodied action, and interactive world systems. WorldFoundry unifies model and benchmark discovery, runtime and asset preparation, execution orchestration, artifact management, and interactive visualization, while modality-specific adapters preserve native inputs, execution semantics, output representations, and evaluation protocols. Explicit manifests, durable artifact contracts, and evidence-aware scorecards separate execution readiness from evaluative claims, making each claim traceable to its supporting artifacts. The current catalog contains 270 model entries, 74 benchmarks, and 62 registered metric entries, with integration readiness and execution evidence recorded separately for each entry. By coupling world modeling with evidence-grounded executable infrastructure, WorldFoundry enables reproducible comparison of persistent, controllable dynamics across heterogeneous systems, advancing the field from perceptual synthesis toward measurable world intelligence.

title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts

details.title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
details.abstract: ReproBridge starts from a simple question: when a coding agent reproduces a paper, how much of its success comes from the released artifacts, and how much from the agent filling in what the paper and code leave implicit? What we built Refined reproducible artifact (RRA): refined code, environment setup, experiment launchers, and a reproduction guide that records the rationale behind each setting and repair. ReproBridge: an agent workflow that constructs RRAs from a paper and its official repository (Specify → Execute → Preserve, with an independent Reviewer). ReproBridge-Bench: 1,029 tasks from 387 experiments across 36 ICML 2026 papers, each anchored by five human-verified reference scores. Key results (four coding agents, fresh sessions, raw code vs. RRA) Mean success 76.4% → 92.6%; downstream API spending −19.7% Cross-model spread 21.6 → 3.9 pp; all four models above 90% Every component matters in the ablation, code and environment the most External check on CORE-Bench Hard: capsule success 62.2% → 73.3%, cost per successful capsule 4.34 How we evaluate research agents Published scores are single observations → compatibility intervals from five independent human reproductions, applied in both directions. Numbers can match for the wrong reasons → an Auditor traces each value to output files, execution records and scripts; against two human reviewers it reaches 88.6% precision / 79.5% recall (818 outcomes). Hold the task fixed and vary only the handoff → this separates artifact quality from agent ability. 🌐 Project page with interactive results, a 36-paper explorer and case studies: https://wyyyb.github.io/reprobridge_website/ Code and data are under internal review and will be released once approved. Happy to answer questions!

title: Flide: Accelerating Decision Inference with Exact State Forking

details.title: Flide: Accelerating Decision Inference with Exact State Forking
details.abstract: Hi everyone! I'm one of the authors of Flide. We built Flide from scratch, an open-source inference engine for Jev-like decision models. The key idea is exact state forking, which allows multiple questions to share computation while preserving exact decision semantics. In our testing, Flide achieves up to 9.5× faster inference than vLLM and SGLang. We support 30+ open-source decision models on Decision Index 0.4.1 , with support for more models on the way. Get started with one line: pip install flide Code: https://github.com/OmniJev/Flide Docs: https://docs.flide.org/ Arxiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.42148 We'd love to hear your feedback, questions, and ideas!

title: TRIO: Task Refinement with Individual Optimization for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

details.title: TRIO: Task Refinement with Individual Optimization for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
details.abstract: Can three specialized agents make RAG more accurate than a single powerful reasoning model? 🚀 Introducing TRIO , a multi-agent RAG framework that improves retrieval-augmented reasoning through specialized agent optimization. TRIO jointly coordinates three agents, each optimized for a distinct role: Query Agent: Learns to retrieve evidence that directly improves downstream answer quality. Judge Agent: Determines whether the retrieved evidence is sufficient to answer the question. Answer Agent: Develops robust reasoning capabilities over noisy retrieved contexts through reward-driven curriculum learning. Key highlights: Top average Exact Match across five QA benchmarks , outperforming strong RAG baselines, including Search-R1. 76.6% accuracy on unseen PubMedQA , demonstrating promising cross-domain generalization. Strong performance with compact 4B and 8B models , highlighting the potential of specialized multi-agent optimization. Key insight: Effective RAG depends on how well retrieval, evidence assessment, and answer generation work together. Optimizing each agent for its specific role can substantially improve end-to-end reasoning.

title: JoVox: Joint Hierarchical Flow Matching for Lightweight Voxel Generation

details.title: JoVox: Joint Hierarchical Flow Matching for Lightweight Voxel Generation
details.abstract: JoVox generates voxel structures with one discrete flow matching model that learns all hierarchy levels jointly (4³ → 16³ → 64³), instead of one level at a time. Compared with TRELLIS.2 using the same backbone: 8× training throughput, 1/15 FLOPs per forward pass (0.82 vs. 12.2 TFLOPs) trained on 4 H100 GPUs instead of 32 11% lower Chamfer distance on 1000 Toys4k objects (image-conditioned) Code, the 64³ model and an image-to-mesh script (via the second stage of TRELLIS.2) are released.

title: Horizon-Scalable Q-Learning

details.title: Horizon-Scalable Q-Learning
details.abstract: Learning accurate off-policy state-action value functions (Q-functions) from offline datasets becomes harder as the task horizon grows. One-step temporal-difference (TD) learning bootstraps after every transition, so small per-step errors accumulate along the horizon, and early states can be badly misvalued even when the TD loss is small. Multi-step TD shortens this chain by following the dataset trajectory for several steps; however, since the behavior policy is often suboptimal, every followed action adds a bias, and no fixed number of steps suits a whole trajectory. In this paper, we propose Horizon-Scalable Q-Learning (HQL), a simple method that enables accurate long-horizon value learning by automatically balancing between one-step and multi-step returns. HQL extends a target through a dataset action only when the critic values it at least as highly as the best-of-N actions sampled from the BC policy, and otherwise falls back to a one-step target. We show that this rule is a principled off-policy correction that needs no action densities, which makes HQL compatible with expressive flow and diffusion policies. Experiments show that HQL avoids the failures of both one-step and multi-step TD on a combination-lock task across horizons, and outperforms prior horizon-reduction methods on long-horizon OGBench and OCBench tasks.

title: PhysioWave-T: Token-Efficient Wavelet Foundation Models for Biosignals

details.title: PhysioWave-T: Token-Efficient Wavelet Foundation Models for Biosignals
details.abstract: We introduce PhysioWave-T, an efficient biosignal foundation model for EEG, ECG, and surface EMG. Scaling across these signals requires handling diverse recording setups and varying signal quality. Our Dynamic Scale Folding adapts to heterogeneous channel counts and sampling rates, delivering up to 7.2× faster inference and 12.7× lower memory usage. For multimodal applications, Reliability-Aware Latent Fusion dynamically weights independently pretrained encoders according to signal quality, improving robustness in tasks such as wearable seizure detection. Together, these advances bring scalable biosignal modeling closer to practical deployment.

title: AutoVend: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Autonomous Vending Operations

details.title: AutoVend: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Autonomous Vending Operations
details.abstract: 🤖 Can an LLM agent run a vending business for 180 days? Many commercial tasks end when a transaction is completed. Running a business is different: today’s decisions determine tomorrow’s stock availability, costs, and cash position. We introduce AutoVend , a benchmark where one LLM agent operates 20 vending machines across five site types for 180 simulated days through a digital operating interface. 📦 Digital decisions meet physical constraints The agent chooses products, sets prices, orders inventory, and plans replenishment. A data-grounded simulator combines heterogeneous local demand with shared inventory and cash, procurement lead times, paid on-site replenishment, product expiration, and recurring operating costs. Stock in the warehouse cannot satisfy customers until it reaches machine shelves. 🔍 What does AutoVend test? Coordinating shared resources across sites with different demand. Planning procurement and replenishment under delays and costs. Using accumulated feedback to revise operating decisions over time. 📊 What do we find? Four of five evaluated LLM agents fall short of a rule-based inventory-control baseline. Better individual operating metrics do not consistently translate into stronger economic returns, and accounting for inference costs changes model rankings. AutoVend examines whether agents can turn repeated decisions into sustained business performance—and helps diagnose where that process breaks down.

title: FlyHash for LLM Agent Memory: An Empirical Validation and a New Application

details.title: FlyHash for LLM Agent Memory: An Empirical Validation and a New Application
details.abstract: Hi everyone, I'm one of the authors. We tested FlyHash, a fruit-fly-inspired sparse hash, against SimHash for retrieving memories in LLM agents, using matched bit budgets and a labeled benchmark we released (6,000 memories, 150 queries). Main result: at equal bits, FlyHash ranks the right memories much higher (mAP 0.271 vs 0.105 at k=32). The caveats are in the paper too: at equal bits its codes are larger and slower to compare, and an HNSW index beats both hash methods at ordinary scale. So it's a quality-per-bit result, not a drop-in replacement. There's an interactive demo that ranks one question at a time (the GIF is one of 12 random questions, where FlyHash wins 11), and the code reproduces every number. Critique and questions are welcome.

title: dNaViT: Discrete Codes are General-Purpose Visual Representations

details.title: dNaViT: Discrete Codes are General-Purpose Visual Representations
details.abstract: We introduce dNaViT: Discrete Codes are General-Purpose Visual Representations. dNaViT is a native-resolution visual tokenizer that combines residual modulation, grouped product quantization, and progressive three-stage training to preserve both semantic and pixel-level information. Its shared discrete visual codes support high-fidelity reconstruction, visual understanding, generation, and editing. Code and the project page are now available!

title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation

details.title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
details.abstract: Trained action policies write manipulation skill into network weights, tying what is learned to the distribution it is learned from. In-context learning (ICL) avoids this coupling but has not matched trained policies, because a demonstration recorded in another scene carries no feedback from the world the robot currently faces. We observe that what an agent learns in context is semantic, recording task steps and object roles rather than visual appearance, so experience gathered in one world transfers to another. Based on this insight, we propose World In-Context Learning (WICL), a paradigm in which a frozen model starts from a demonstration, rehearses the task in a world such as a simulator, and writes the feedback into its context rather than its weights. We build RoboScript, a modular infrastructure that implements WICL for agentic manipulation. From a single demonstration, RoboScript learns each task through rehearsal in simulation, freezes the learned knowledge as a Task Memory, and deploys the frozen memory on new scenes with data isolation that ensures every deployment input is available on a real robot. On all 50 tasks of RoboTwin 2.0, RoboScript reaches 83.4% mean success across clean and randomized settings with one demonstration per task and no gradient updates, exceeding the strongest trained action policy by over 20 points. The method generalizes across visual distributions, improves through reflection, scales with the foundation model, and transfers to a physical dual-arm robot through cross-embodiment memory adaptation. With a world in the loop, a robot can learn a manipulation task in its context as well as it learns one in its weights. All code is available.

title: Few-Step Streaming Video Generation via Condition Shifting

details.title: Few-Step Streaming Video Generation via Condition Shifting
details.abstract: Hi everyone! We’re sharing our latest work extending APEX from image generation to few-step streaming video generation . Condition Shifting lets the generator and fake estimator share one network, removing the separate fake-score network and reducing training overhead. On 180-second videos , APEX achieves +30.0% net human preference for instruction following over S2-Avatar. Under matched training settings, it reduces peak GPU memory by 4.4% and average iteration time by 9.2% compared with DMD. We welcome feedback and HF upvotes! 🤗 📑 arXiv 🎬 Project Page 💻 Code

title: DepthGraft: Structural Regularization through Hierarchical Cross-Layer KV Reconstruction

details.title: DepthGraft: Structural Regularization through Hierarchical Cross-Layer KV Reconstruction
details.abstract: Scaling depth is a key route to stronger large language models, but Pre-LN architectures often suffer from depth-wise information dilution, limiting the effective use of deep layers. While cross-layer connectivity has proven effective at mitigating this problem, existing designs usually introduce additional computation or memory access. We revisit cross-layer KV sharing as an efficient form of such connectivity. Beyond cache compression, each KV reuse edge creates a direct gradient path from deep layers to source KV projections, turning KV sharing into an implicit structural regularizer for KV representation geometry. We provide a systematic analysis of this mechanism, showing that proper sharing topologies sharpen key retrieval directions while enriching the value content subspace, whereas existing adjacent or global-anchor designs do not fully exploit this effect. Motivated by this, we propose DepthGraft, a hierarchical KV-sharing architecture that reconstructs deep-layer KV from stride-aligned shallow-middle source pairs. DepthGraft distributes non-local gradient flow across source layers, while preserving prefill early completion and reducing KV cache by roughly one third. Experiments on dense and MoE models from 0.5B to 16B parameters show consistent downstream improvements under both GQA and MLA. Notably, on the 16B MoE model, DepthGraft achieves a 7.0% absolute improvement on MMLU-Pro, along with gains of 6.6% on CMMLU and 6.4% on C3. These results validate the potential of DepthGraft as a scalable design for large-scale pretraining. The project page is available at https://github.com/jianke0604/DepthGraft .

title: PhysOPSD: Code as Privilege for Physically Plausible Video Generation

details.title: PhysOPSD: Code as Privilege for Physically Plausible Video Generation
details.abstract: Empowering generation with coding agents: Recent approaches use coding agents to replace parts of the video generation process. We explore how coding agents can empower the generator itself. Executable code supplies structured physical supervision during post-training. The resulting capabilities stay in the model, with no simulator required at inference .

title: ExRL: Sample-Efficient Online Adaptation of Long-Chunk Policies via Execution Length Control

details.title: ExRL: Sample-Efficient Online Adaptation of Long-Chunk Policies via Execution Length Control
details.abstract: ExRL enables sample-efficient online improvement of long-chunk robot policies by RL. It learns how much of each predicted chunk to execute using a lightweight RL policy, improving task performance across simulation and the real world.

title: DexForesight: Grounding Dexterous Policies with Implicit Spatial Foresight

details.title: DexForesight: Grounding Dexterous Policies with Implicit Spatial Foresight
details.abstract: Excited to share DexForesight , our latest work from the Sharpa Foundation Model Team ! Project Page: https://dexforesight.github.io/ Most existing dexterous manipulation models rely primarily on RGB observations. However, even in simple pick-and-place tasks, the robot's fingers—the parts that actually interact with objects—are often occluded by the object or the back of the hand, making them difficult to observe from both third-person and wrist-mounted cameras. Even with depth observations, it remains challenging for the model to understand the hand's physical structure, geometry, and how it interacts with the environment. DexForesight addresses this by injecting hand geometry into a world model , enabling it to explicitly imagine the future motion of the dexterous hand and its interactions with the environment. More importantly, DexForesight transfers this capability to a standard VLA policy through learned World Queries . This allows a policy that takes only images and language as input to develop hand-aware spatial imagination during high-level planning, without explicitly generating future observations at inference time! Check out our project!

title: Predictive Surprise as Self-Grounding Concept Bottleneck for Interpretable Time Series

details.title: Predictive Surprise as Self-Grounding Concept Bottleneck for Interpretable Time Series
details.abstract: CONCEPTTIME uses predictive surprise from a frozen probabilistic forecaster to jointly identify segment boundaries and learn an interpretable vocabulary of temporal concepts. A lightweight classifier predicts from the concept sequence, while distance to the nearest concept provides a reliability signal for abstaining when evidence is weak. Across 17 benchmarks, it matches state-of-the-art black-box accuracy and outperforms interpretable baselines without expert annotations or language model calls.

title: Learning to Act with World Models by Valuing What Comes Next

details.title: Learning to Act with World Models by Valuing What Comes Next
details.abstract: TL;DR. A sparse terminal reward says little about individual steps, yet each state transition can change the chances of success long before the reward arrives. WM-PPO learns from this information: a world model trained on real transitions predicts what each sampled action would change, and PPO's own critic values the predicted successor by the current policy's probability of success. Highlights Learning from actions that were never executed. For every action the policy samples, executed or not, the value of its predicted successor enters training twice: comparisons among the candidates give the policy auxiliary advantages (policy channel), and their mean gives the critic a one-step target (value channel). Grounded in real outcomes. A shared gate weights both channels by how reliably comparisons with similar value margins predicted real branch outcomes earlier in training. A minimal addition to PPO. The world model is the only learned component added. No teacher model or privileged information is used, and only the policy runs at inference. Results. With a comparable number of real environment steps, success rises from PPO's 63.5% to 87.5% on ALFWorld and from 39.3% to 52.9% on ScienceWorld. WM-PPO matches the strongest PPO refinements we tested on ALFWorld, exceeds the best of them by 6.5 points on ScienceWorld, and also surpasses the teacher-based methods we tested. On text Sokoban, it reaches 87.0% against 77.3% for ProAct's MC-PPO. Behavior. The trained policy more often completes prerequisite steps, such as heating, cooling or cleaning an object, before placing it or committing to an answer. 📄 Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12200 · 💻 Code: https://github.com/nuskonghou/wm-ppo · 🤗 Checkpoints: https://huggingface.co/nuskonghou/wm-ppo

title: Is Your Robot's Memory Just a Clock? Temporal Shortcuts in Memory-Augmented VLA Policies

details.title: Is Your Robot's Memory Just a Clock? Temporal Shortcuts in Memory-Augmented VLA Policies
details.abstract: We asked a robot to repeat a task three times. Two 5-second pauses made it stop after two. On RoboMME, those pauses cut a released memory VLA’s success from 47/50 to 16/50. Hide the same pause frames from memory, and success returns to 45/50. The surprising part: removing timestamps does not fix it. A memory sampled by time still gives uneventful frames a share of its slots. Event-indexed memory recovers much of the loss without retraining. Code · Five trained checkpoints

title: Ensemble Routing for Prompt-Adaptive Cost-Aware LLM Inference

details.title: Ensemble Routing for Prompt-Adaptive Cost-Aware LLM Inference
details.abstract: Most LLM routing approaches select a single model per prompt, while ensembling introduces a different question: which models should we combine, and how many are actually worth invoking? In this paper, we introduce PISA, a cost-aware single-model router, and PISA-E, which extends routing to ensembles with prompt-adaptive composition and size. PISA-E estimates ensemble utility from individual model capability predictions, without requiring ensemble-specific training. It then selects the models to invoke based on the prompt and a configurable cost–quality preference. We evaluate both methods across four routing benchmarks under in-distribution and out-of-distribution settings. PISA achieves the highest macro-average cost–performance hypervolume among the evaluated single-model routers. PISA-E achieves the highest macro-average ensemble task performance when prioritizing quality, while also offering operating points with higher performance at approximately 36% (ID) and 25% (OOD) lower average inference cost than the strongest competing ensembles. Feedback and discussion are welcome, particularly on the ensemble-selection formulation and adaptive ensemble cardinality.

title: BirdDreams: Joint Perspective and BEV Video Generation for a Plausible, Reactive Driving World Model

details.title: BirdDreams: Joint Perspective and BEV Video Generation for a Plausible, Reactive Driving World Model
details.abstract: BirdDreams: A driving world model with accurate ego control and traffic that can react. BirdDreams is a driving world model that generates driving video and a bird’s-eye view of the scene from a single camera image.  It follows input ego trajectories precisely while predicting how surrounding traffic reacts to ego motion.

title: On the Design of Hyper-Connections: Simplification, Stability, and Scalability

details.title: On the Design of Hyper-Connections: Simplification, Stability, and Scalability
details.abstract: We introduce SimpleHC, one of the fastest Hyper-Connections variants to date, reducing repeated memory access through a simpler design. It adds just 2.4% training overhead at the largest tested width while maintaining competitive performance with mHC at 15B and 30B MoE scales.

title: G-STAR: Group-Scaled Token Capacity for Deeply Compressed Autoregressive Generation

details.title: G-STAR: Group-Scaled Token Capacity for Deeply Compressed Autoregressive Generation
details.abstract: Discrete autoregressive models offer a scalable framework for image generation. However, they face a fundamental trade-off: long token sequences preserve representation quality but slow generation, while aggressive spatial compression reduces representation capacity. Based on product quantization, we show that, under a fixed nominal information budget, group size should scale quadratically with the per-axis spatial compression factor. Building on this principle, we propose GSTAR, a spatial--group co-scaling framework that enables 32x and even effective 64x compression while preserving strong reconstruction, understanding, and generation performance. Since larger groups introduce intra-group dependencies that must be modeled efficiently, we analyze their impact on inference latency and generation quality and introduce a semi-autoregressive decoder that combines parallel feature computation with lightweight causal modeling. With these designs, our highly compressed models perform competitively with leading models across five representative text-to-image benchmarks (GenEval, DPG-Bench, PRISM, LongText-Bench, and Qwen-Image-Bench). At 1024x1024resolution, our model delivers a 20x speedup over prior discrete autoregressive models, generating each image in 2.5 seconds on a single NVIDIA H200. Together, these results show that highly compressed discrete representations can enable high-quality autoregressive generation at low latency.

title: From Large Language Models to Efficient System One Models via Adaptive Computation

details.title: From Large Language Models to Efficient System One Models via Adaptive Computation
details.abstract: Transferring LLMs into System One decision models typically replaces the language modeling head with a decision head while retaining the full backbone, making every decision pay for all layers. Yet it remains unclear how much depth such decisions require. We find that decision information is concentrated in intermediate layers, with early layers building essential features and the final six layers removable without loss, while independently trained smaller models largely mimic the full model rather than developing specialized decision capabilities. These findings suggest that efficiency requires not simply smaller backbones, but shared computation across different depths. Building on this, we propose NESTONE, which jointly trains a full model with prefix submodels that share its final layers and decision head through self-distillation. A lightweight gate reads the hidden state at each exit to determine whether additional computation is needed, allowing one model to operate at multiple layers. Across seven decision benchmarks, our approach matches or outperforms independently trained models at every depth, while achieving better accuracy-efficiency trade-offs through adaptive computation.

title: G-STAR: Group-Scaled Token Capacity for Deeply Compressed Autoregressive Generation

details.title: G-STAR: Group-Scaled Token Capacity for Deeply Compressed Autoregressive Generation
details.abstract: Discrete autoregressive models offer a scalable framework for image generation. However, they face a fundamental trade-off: long token sequences preserve representation quality but slow generation, while aggressive spatial compression reduces representation capacity. Based on product quantization, we show that, under a fixed nominal information budget, group size should scale quadratically with the per-axis spatial compression factor. Building on this principle, we propose GSTAR, a spatial--group co-scaling framework that enables 32x and even effective 64x compression while preserving strong reconstruction, understanding, and generation performance. Since larger groups introduce intra-group dependencies that must be modeled efficiently, we analyze their impact on inference latency and generation quality and introduce a semi-autoregressive decoder that combines parallel feature computation with lightweight causal modeling. With these designs, our highly compressed models perform competitively with leading models across five representative text-to-image benchmarks (GenEval, DPG-Bench, PRISM, LongText-Bench, and Qwen-Image-Bench). At 1024x1024resolution, our model delivers a 20x speedup over prior discrete autoregressive models, generating each image in 2.5 seconds on a single NVIDIA H200. Together, these results show that highly compressed discrete representations can enable high-quality autoregressive generation at low latency.

title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents

details.title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
details.abstract: Decision models output typed decisions (e.g., a probability over candidate actions), so the same model can act as an Actor (choose actions), a Judge (evaluate actions already taken), or a Teacher (score every action to provide step-level rewards for RL). Prior work mostly evaluates them as actors. We ask: can a model that acts poorly still teach well? 🔍 Key findings On ALFWorld, we compare 3 decision models and 3 general LLMs. As actors, all six get pulled toward an easier subgoal and skip a prerequisite one. As judges with the full trajectory, the same models correctly credit the steps that advance that prerequisite. What separates useful from useless actions is judging whether each step helped, not predicting whether the task will succeed. ⚡ As a teacher, our JEV gives step-level signals to a Qwen2.5-1.5B policy trained with GRPO: ALFWorld: 72.8% → 82.9% WebShop: 56.8% → 71.4% Our takeaway: judging an action after the episode reveals consequences that acting can only anticipate, so a weak actor can still be a strong teacher. 🌐 Project page: https://zjureal.com/decision-agents/ 💻 Code: https://github.com/ZJU-REAL/decision-agents

title: Ropedia Xperience 2: A Gold Standard for Scaling Physical AI Environments and Behaviors

details.title: Ropedia Xperience 2: A Gold Standard for Scaling Physical AI Environments and Behaviors
details.abstract: Introducing Xperience 2 from Ropedia: a gold standard for scaling Physical AI environments and behaviors. Real-robot data is expensive. DROID's 350 hours of demonstrations took 50 operators a full year, and a real robot can't retry a task the way it can in simulation. Xperience 2 starts from people instead. Operators record first-person video together with hand and full-body motion while doing everyday tasks in real scenes. Every scene is also 3D scanned, and each recording is aligned to its scan, so the video, the motion and the 3D space share one coordinate frame. From this capture, we build simulation-ready scenes, robot trajectories and long-horizon task data, with no robot on site. The release: 1,500+ scenes, 4,000+ recordings, 74 tasks, and three benchmarks.

title: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding

details.title: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding
details.abstract: How multimodal language models should encode visual input remains up for debate. Most models use a pretrained vision encoder, while some recent recipes train the encoder from scratch with the language model or remove it entirely. Vision encoders bundle together three design choices: a visual prior from upstream pretraining, dedicated vision capacity, and pre-fusion placement of that capacity (i.e., before the multimodal backbone). Because published models also differ in data, architecture, and compute, comparing them cannot isolate the effect of each choice. We disentangle these choices via a controlled framework where we pretrain all models from scratch on common data and compare them on visual question answering and language benchmarks at matched lifetime compute. We find that the visual prior is not necessary; an encoder trained jointly from scratch is on par with a pretrained one, without a separate training stage. What matters instead is dedicated vision capacity: an encoder-free model trails on visual understanding even when its backbone is enlarged by the encoder's parameter count. Yet that capacity need not precede multimodal fusion, as vision-only modules added in-fusion to early backbone layers perform comparably to a pre-fusion encoder and can lower time to first token. These results also hold across backbone sizes, when encoder pretraining is treated as free, and when starting from a pretrained language model. Overall, our findings favor dedicated vision capacity trained jointly with the backbone and placed early within it. https://unbundling.github.io/

title: Consensus Capture in Reference-Based UAV Video Stabilization: A Benchmark on Dynamic Urban Scenes

details.title: Consensus Capture in Reference-Based UAV Video Stabilization: A Benchmark on Dynamic Urban Scenes
details.abstract: Reference-frame stabilization registers every frame of a hovering-drone video onto one reference frame, and its registration pipelines are usually picked on feature-matching benchmarks where only the camera moves. Over a busy intersection, vehicles moving together can pull the robust homography toward their own motion (consensus capture), while inlier counts and ratios still look normal. We measure this with a two-part benchmark: Static: ten pipelines scored under exactly known homographies on 4K aerial frames, with tuning on a site-disjoint split. Dynamic: real hovers selected from the video alone, at an offline and a real-time budget, scored against a reference audited with manually annotated ground control points. Unmasked ORB is captured on 28 of 304 real-time pairs; its captured estimates have a median corner error of 18.8 px with typical inlier statistics. Masking removes capture for every pipeline and leaves the leading pipelines unchanged. Released: the code on GitHub , the benchmark data with all results on Zenodo , and Songdo Vision OBB , with 274,190 oriented boxes on 5,419 4K drone frames.

The harness we end up with is simple and goes from 29.7 to 50.3, with no learned policy, self-improvement loop or task-specific tuning. title: HiVe-Mem: Interleaving Horizontal Memory Expansion and Vertical Evidence Composition for Multimodal Agents

details.title: HiVe-Mem: Interleaving Horizontal Memory Expansion and Vertical Evidence Composition for Multimodal Agents
details.abstract: As multimodal agents accumulate increasingly long interaction histories, effectively retrieving and utilizing past information becomes critical for long-term interaction. Existing memory systems typically rely on semantic retrieval over compressed memories and expose predefined representations, which may miss relevant memories and overlook heterogeneous evidence needs across queries. We introduce \textbf{\hivemem}, a multimodal memory framework that interleaves \textbf{\textsc{H}}or\textbf{\textsc{i}}zontal Memory Expansion with \textbf{\textsc{Ve}}rtical Evidence Composition. For horizontal memory expansion, \hivemem organizes memory episodes into a relational graph using textual and visual anchors, expanding semantically retrieved seeds with related neighbors to recover complementary information. For vertical evidence composition, each retrieved memory retains multiple evidence forms, including compact summaries, captions, grounded visual views, raw images, and interaction history. A lightweight trainable selector independently composes an evidence subset for each retrieved memory, enabling query-adaptive utilization of heterogeneous multimodal information. This two-dimensional design jointly broadens memory coverage and adapts the evidence contributed by individual memories. Experiments across three multimodal memory benchmarks show that \hivemem consistently improves task performance across base models while reducing token consumption by about 90% compared with the most efficient competing multimodal baselines.

title: Agent-R^2: Scaling Agents for Realistic Productivity Work via Real-Source Data Synthesis

details.title: Agent-R^2: Scaling Agents for Realistic Productivity Work via Real-Source Data Synthesis
details.abstract: Real productivity work means turning heterogeneous files (annual reports, spreadsheets, PDFs) into deliverables with the right format and evidence. LLM agents still struggle here: workflows are long, files are messy, and success criteria are fine-grained. A key bottleneck is the lack of scalable training data that captures real work intent, real file environments, and deliverable-level evaluation. 💡 We propose Agent-R² , a real-source data synthesis framework for cowork agents. Starting from occupational activity seeds, it extracts file-oriented workflows from web corpora, retrieves and verifies real public attachments, then synthesizes instructions, fine-grained rubrics, and reference deliverables in a sandbox. 🛠 Data 4k task instances distilled from 10k web candidates Avg. 2.51 real multi-format attachments and 15.3 deliverable-level rubrics per task Expert trajectories: avg. 18.0 steps, 41.8k tokens Rubric-based verification: unreasonable rubrics are revised, and unmet ones trigger one more round of expert revision ⚡ Results (Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 → SFT + rubric-based RL → Agent-R²-4B) GDPval: 51.0% Pass@1, surpassing Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507 (48.0%), +18.6 over the 4B base OfficeQA: 2.2% → 14.8% Pass@1, also above Qwen3-235B (13.8%) Less shortcut behavior: completion rate reaches 90.9%, with more effective tool steps Ablations: real files beat synthetic ones (43.3 vs. 41.4), with 2.54× more expert tool calls (20.4 vs. 8.0); removing the rubric reward drops RL from 51.0 to 49.5 💻 Code: https://github.com/ZJU-REAL/Agent-R2 🤗 Model: https://huggingface.co/teng-pan/Agent-R2-4B

title: Evidence-Guided Recovery for AI Agents with Ambiguous Tool Outcomes and Partial Execution

details.title: Evidence-Guided Recovery for AI Agents with Ambiguous Tool Outcomes and Partial Execution
details.abstract: Tool timeouts can leave AI agents facing ambiguous tool outcomes and partial execution: an action may have failed, committed or remained in flight while other workflow steps have already completed. We formulate evidence-guided task recovery over approved obligations, provider capabilities and states compatible with public evidence. A shared admissibility check handles key expiry, authorization timing, dependencies and residual effects; a terminal certificate separates actual goal satisfaction from publicly supported safe completion. The known-model implementation combines standard observation-contingent planning with a separately implemented effect-history adjudicator. In a finite study of 37 assignments, planning and three active controls each certify 28 completions; four saved synthetic fee units incur additional computation. A preregistered assignment-held-out comparison then evaluates planning advice against evidence prompting with two local model bundles. Across 58 paired units in 19 previously developed task families, advice certifies 30 completions versus 9, a 36.2-percentage-point difference (exact family sign-flip p=0.0078), using 272 proposals versus 399. All 116 trajectories pass independent replay. Both models exhibit a positive completion difference. The comparison measures the evaluated advice interface under a common shield; search-versus-rule advice requires a separate matched comparison. Unknown and handoff outcomes remain explicit, with guarantees tied to the declared provider capabilities rather than arbitrary third-party exactly-once execution.

title: Do Multimodal Models Decide Consistently on Equivalent Optical Spectra?

details.title: Do Multimodal Models Decide Consistently on Equivalent Optical Spectra?
details.abstract: A spectrum can be given to a model as a table in nanometers or as a plot in photon energy, and the decision should not depend on which one it sees. When the data needed for an answer are missing, the model should say so. We test representation invariance and abstention on measured optical spectra of silicon metasurfaces (MOCLIP) and gold nanoparticles, with labels computed from the data. Each spectrum is shown as four tables (nm, μm, scientific notation, eV) and two plots (nm, eV), and partial spectra remove data inside or outside the queried range. We evaluate the decision models d3-nano and Jev 1.13, three GPT-6 Luna configurations and the Qwen3.5-2B base model. Changing only the representation moves accuracy by up to 41 percentage points within one model, mostly on photon-energy tables and plots. With the same evidence, asking in photon energy instead of wavelength helps some model-view pairs by 16-50 points and hurts others by up to 25. When the relevant extremum is removed, unadapted models rarely answer "undetermined". LoRA fine-tuning of d3-nano improves comparisons on the trained table formats, but much of its gain on unanswerable questions comes from a shortcut: it abstains whenever the input is truncated. Training with answerable truncations avoids the shortcut in all six seeds, with a 90-100 point gap between abstention after inside and outside cuts on held-out structures; with the same amount of extra original-task data, five of six seeds keep the shortcut. On gold spectra the two training sets perform similarly. Multimodal language models used for scientific decisions should be tested on equivalent representations and on missing evidence, not only on average accuracy. We release the tasks, per-response results and analysis code.

title: Experience-Handoff Reinforcement Learning for Recursive Self-Improvement

details.title: Experience-Handoff Reinforcement Learning for Recursive Self-Improvement
details.abstract: Why not train an agent's weights inside the harness it runs in? Reinforcement learning (RL) is the standard way to train LLM agents, and it boils a whole attempt down to one reward number. Everything the agent saw along the way is thrown out: error logs, tool outputs, constraints it discovered. Harnesses like ACE (Agentic Context Engineering) keep that information. The model reflects on each attempt and writes notes in a playbook, which its next attempt reads. But the model was never trained to write those notes, so a small model gains little from its own edits. In our new paper, Experience-Handoff Reinforcement Learning for Recursive Self-Improvement, we combine the two. We keep the ACE harness fixed and train one model in three roles: the actor that does the task, the reflector that draws lessons from an attempt, and the curator that edits the playbook. Our method, ACE-RL, scores each playbook edit by running the next attempt with it and checking the task reward. Each role is compared only against other outputs of the same role, which keeps its learning signal stable. We credit each rollout's contribution to the final task reward to get reward group for each component. We found that ACE-RL reaches the highest held-out reward of all methods we tested: PPO, GRPO, ERL, and end-to-end PPO through the harness. The gains last even after the cutoff that we give during the train. We trained with 3 attempts per task, and ACE-RL stays ahead of GRPO up to 8 attempts. Training only the actor isn't enough. A GRPO-trained model placed in the same harness after 8 attempts ends up below where it gets by simply sampling 8 times. Our takeaway: agent training should improve the agent's actions, and also the notes it leaves for its future attempts.

title: Structured Confidence Perturbation via Fisher Geometry for Adversarial Training

details.title: Structured Confidence Perturbation via Fisher Geometry for Adversarial Training
details.abstract: Adversarial training is often plagued by "pseudo-attacks"—perturbations that significantly increase the loss value but fail to truly alter the model's confidence structure. To address this, we propose two complementary approaches to directly attack and defend against confidence structure deformation. First, building upon the traditional loss maximization perspective, we introduce a hybrid objective that integrates cross-entropy and KL divergence, encouraging adversarial examples to simultaneously disrupt prediction accuracy and distribution consistency. Second, we geometrically reconstruct adversarial training by generating perturbations that maximize the distribution distance on the confidence manifold. Theoretical analysis shows that the optimal perturbation direction aligns with the principal eigenvectors of the Fisher information matrix. We also propose an efficient algorithm to avoid high-dimensional matrix computations. Experiments on multiple datasets and model architectures demonstrate that our method outperforms existing methods in adversarial robustness and robust transferability, particularly excelling in structural perturbations within high-confidence regions.

title: Humanized but Still True? Auditing Facts and Detection in AI-Text Humanizers

details.title: Humanized but Still True? Auditing Facts and Detection in AI-Text Humanizers
details.abstract: AI "humanizers" rewrite machine-generated text so that detectors classify it as human-written. Public leaderboards score evasion and embedding similarity, but not whether checkable details survive. We check whether numbers, dates, person and organization names, and quoted spans survive each rewrite, using a rule-based checker validated by two AI annotators (precision 0.84-1.00, recall 0.93-0.95; no human annotation). In the October 2026 cycle of a public humanizer leaderboard, all 11 commercial tools changed or dropped at least one of these units in 35-65% of the documents that contained one. Most changes were to quoted spans; counting numbers and names alone, 10 of the 11 tools still altered at least one in 20% or more of the documents. The September 2026 cycle was similar (19-50%). An open 12B humanizer kept at least 97% of numbers and names in fact-dense U.S. federal agency text, but reworded 67-78% of the quoted spans, against its own prompt. Unit retention and detector evasion were not clearly related across tools (Spearman rho = -0.46, 95% CI -0.65 to 0.08), and the open model's four released files (two of them quantization-aware low-bit files) did not show the pre-registered monotone trade-off. On federal texts with matched human, AI-styled and humanized versions, a general-purpose decision model, Jev, asked a single zero-shot question, separated human originals from humanized rewrites with AUROC 0.864 (0.827-0.902), 0.18-0.22 higher than Binoculars, Fast-DetectGPT and the adversarially trained RADAR, while calling 24% of the human originals AI at a 0.5 threshold. On the AI-styled rewrites by 2026 models, both perplexity-based detectors scored below chance (AUROC 0.37 and 0.39), also with line breaks removed. Hypotheses, data rules and analyses were frozen before the main runs; two earlier data contacts are disclosed. We release the checker and the per-item results.

title: EgoX: Egocentric Cross-Embodiment Manipulation with Embodiment Dreaming

details.title: EgoX: Egocentric Cross-Embodiment Manipulation with Embodiment Dreaming
details.abstract: Generalist manipulation policies can benefit from the complementary experience of humans, real robots, and simulated agents. However, differences in morphology, sensing, and control interfaces make it difficult to learn effectively from their combined demonstrations. We introduce EgoX, an egocentric cross-embodiment learning framework that organizes heterogeneous demonstrations through semantically corresponding observation and action modalities. EgoX pretrains a Modularized Cross-Embodiment Transformer with Embodiment Dreaming (MXT+) on this mixture and fine-tunes it on target-embodiment demonstrations. Within each embodiment, MXT+ assigns a dedicated tokenizer to each observation modality and a dedicated expert to each action modality, with a Transformer trunk shared across embodiments. A training-only embodiment-dreaming objective predicts latent representations of future visual and proprioceptive states, encouraging the shared trunk to model each embodiment's dynamics. Across 13 task–embodiment pairs spanning five tasks and six robot embodiments, including five physical robots and one simulated humanoid, cross-embodiment pretraining raises MXT+'s average normalized task progress from 0.63 to 0.80 over training from scratch. The gains are particularly pronounced under out-of-distribution conditions, where average task progress increases from 0.53 to 0.77. Ablations demonstrate the benefits of broader pretraining mixtures, modular interfaces, and embodiment dreaming, with dreaming producing more similar latent geometry across embodiments.

title: A frontier machine intelligence for human neuroimaging

details.title: A frontier machine intelligence for human neuroimaging
details.abstract: Neuro-VL is a machine intelligence for human neuroimaging designed to reason over images and clinical context and communicate its interpretations through natural-language conversation. We developed Neuro-VL using nearly 1 million neuroimaging studies from 450,000 patients, comprising 10 million volumetric scans. Neuro-VL employs HLIP as the visual encoder that incorporates a hierarchical attention mechanism inspired by the inherent structure of neuroimaging data. This visual encoder was pretrained using radiology reports to extract semantically rich visual representations from complex neuroimaging studies. Building on these representations, Neuro-VL generates robust radiological interpretations accompanied by auditable reasoning traces. Resources: Neuro-VL code: https://github.com/MLNeurosurg/neuro-vl Model weights: https://huggingface.co/mlinslab/neuro-vl-8b-thinking NeuroBench evaluation benchmark: https://huggingface.co/datasets/mlinslab/neurobench NeuroBench evaluation tools with LLM judges: https://github.com/MLNeurosurg/neurobench

details.abstract: Self-Evolving Multimodal Agents
